newsitem.title: JAPAN: Former Japan state-owned railway has smooth debut.
newsitem.headline: Former Japan state-owned railway has smooth debut.

text.p: West Japan Railway, once part of the state rail network, made its debut on Japan's major stock exchanges on Tuesday, attracting lukewarm buying interest but avoiding the disaster that some market players had feared.

There had been concerns that the offering would pull money out of other shares and depress the market. Investor interest was seen as tentative after problems in previous privatisations of state-owned groups.

At the end of the morning session on the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE), JR West shares were quoted at 366,000 yen ($3,297) up from the offer price of 357,000 yen ($3,216) but below some analysts expectations of around 400,000 yen ($3,603).
The launch did cause shares in its one-time sibling East Japan Railway Co (JR East) to fall and they stayed lower despite a rise in the overall market.
The Nikkei 225-share index was slightly higher, ending the morning 18.37 points up at 21,179.38.
JR East went public in October 1993, becoming Japan's first formerly public railway firm to be floated after the state-owned Japanese National Railway (JNR) was broken up into seven units in 1987.
West Japan Railway is the second of the group to go public. ($1=111 yen)
